Worked example: Harvest Lane's HL · New order → email Tolu scenario, run once with three test rows (HL-0061, HL-0062, HL-0063). Bundle 2 is HL-0062.

Why 4 credits. The Sheets bubble is a polling trigger. It made one check, which costs 1 credit whether it finds nothing or three rows. It found three rows and output three bundles. A module runs once for every bundle that reaches it, so Gmail ran three times: 3 credits. Total: 1 + 3 = 4, the same figure shown for this run in scenario history.

Log line: Test run: bundles per bubble 3 / 3, credits used 4 (1 check + 3 emails).
mistakes: Choosing "all" as the trigger's starting point, so old orders flood the run and the counts no longer show 3 and 3.
Recording bundle 2's values from the Sheets bubble only and never opening the Gmail bubble's input and output.
Saying the run cost 3 credits (one per email) and forgetting the polling check.
Typing real customer names or numbers into the test rows or the log.
b.pass: The log shows both bubble counts (3 and 3), three input and three output values from bundle 2, and the sentence "1 credit for the check plus 3 for the emails = 4", matching scenario history.
b.redo: Send it back if the 4 credits are explained without mentioning the polling check, if the values come from the wrong bundle, or if the figures are guessed rather than read from history.

Worked example: Harvest Lane's Track 1 delivery-fee Zap, rebuilt in Make and run against the same five test orders (Bodija, Challenge, Bodija, Jericho, Challenge).

Zapier (Track 1)Make (Weave Workshop)
Steps / modulesNew row in Orders → Formatter lookup table (area → fee) → Update row → Gmail to ToluWatch New Rows → Update a Row with switch(1.area; "Bodija"; 1500; "Challenge"; 2000; 2500) in the delivery_fee field → Gmail
Test setupCopy of the sheet: Orders_test_zapCopy of the sheet: Orders_test_make
ResultFees 1,500 / 2,000 / 1,500 / 2,500 / 2,000; five emailsSame fees, same five emails (checked row by row)
Usage (from history)10 tasks (Update + Gmail per order; Formatter not counted)11 credits (1 check + 5 updates + 5 emails, one run)
Build time25 minutes15 minutes

Three-line comparison:

  1. Both tools produced identical fees and emails for all five test orders.
  2. Zapier used 10 tasks; Make used 11 credits, because the polling check costs 1 even though the lookup inside the field costs nothing. At hourly checks for 14 hours a day, checking alone adds about 420 credits a month.
  3. Make was quicker to build (15 vs 25 minutes) because switch() replaced a whole Formatter step.

Submit: the table, screenshots of Zap history and scenario history for the test run (no personal data), and the three lines.
mistakes: Running the Zap and the scenario on the same sheet at once, so each tool's updates collide and results can't be compared.
Rebuilding with different logic (a different fee table or missing step), so "identical results" isn't really tested.
Quoting tasks and credits from memory or the pricing page instead of Zap history and scenario history.
Leaving the polling check out of the Make cost, or counting Formatter steps as Zapier tasks.
s.pass: Both tools processed the same five test items with identical outputs, and the three-line comparison gives real task and credit figures from the two histories plus both build times.
s.redo: Send it back if the chosen Zap has fewer than three steps, if outputs differ without explanation, or if the numbers have no history screenshots behind them.

Worked example: Harvest Lane's five Boss 0 automations at December volume (130 orders a day), costed over 30 days with the 2.1 calculator.

AutomationTrigger and scheduleBundles / dayModules per bundleChecking / monthWork / month
1 Order captureInstant webhook1305019,500
2 Payment confirmationInstant webhook (Paystack)1256022,500
3 Hotel daily cycleScheduled 20:00, 21:00, 05:0015290900
4 Friday hotel invoiceWeekly, Friday 09:001 invoice a week (Grand Palm)4416
5 Stock alertDaily 07:0025 products130750
Total124≈ 43,700

Justifications. Orders and payments must react at once, so they use webhooks: no credits spent checking. The hotel cycle runs only at the three times the contract needs. The invoice and stock alert are once-a-week and once-a-day jobs, so a single scheduled run is enough.

Plan. About 43,800 credits a month, plus 20% headroom: about 53,000. Choose the smallest plan on Make's pricing page that covers 53,000 credits, and write its name, its monthly price and the date you checked. Note that AI modules can use extra credits based on token use (2.7), so measure automation 1 in testing.

Biggest saving from going instant: order capture. Polling the form sheet every 15 minutes, all day, would add 2,880 credits a month. The bigger lesson: at December volume, the work dominates, so trimming one module per order saves 3,900 credits a month on order capture alone.

Submit: the table, calculator screenshots for each row, the plan name and price with the date, and these notes.
mistakes: Estimating December with normal-month volumes instead of the Boss 0 figure of 130 orders a day.
Polling the order and payment flows every 15 minutes all day when a webhook would cost nothing to wait.
Writing "1 credit per order" for flows that have five or six modules per bundle.
Naming a plan or price from memory, with no date and no headroom for growth or AI token credits.
g.pass: All five automations have bundles, modules, a trigger type and a one-line reason; the monthly total is added up correctly and matched to a named plan with price and date checked; one automation is named as the best instant-trigger saving, with the credits saved.
g.redo: Send it back if any automation is missing or unjustified, if the arithmetic doesn't add up, or if the plan isn't named or doesn't actually cover the total.
